AMERICAN FORK CITY COUNCIL
JUNE 2, 2026
		WORK SESSION AGENDA




*Notice of Electronic Meeting*
One or more City Council members may be physically absent from this meeting but may participate electronically.

Notice is hereby given that the American Fork City Council will hold a work session on Tuesday, June 2, 2026, in the City Administration Conference Room, located at 51 East Main Street, commencing at 4:00 p.m. The agenda shall be as follows:
WORK SESSION
The purpose of the City Work Sessions is to prepare the City Council for upcoming agenda items on future City Council Meetings. The Work Session is not an action item meeting. No one attending the meeting should rely on any discussion or any perceived consensus as action or authorization. These come only from the City Council Meeting.

1.	Presentation of progress on the American Fork Transit Circulator Study and Polycentric City Master Plan.
2.	Report by Dawna Whiting on the American Fork Victim's Assistance Program.
3.	Discussion on Master Plans, Impact Fee Facility Plans, and Impact Fee Analysis for Culinary Water, Parks, Pressurized Irrigation, Public Safety, Sewer, Storm Drain, and Transportation.

Dated the 28th day of May 2026.

City Recorder

title: Public Hearing
agenda_text:
EAGLE MOUNTAIN CITY COUNCIL
NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARINGS

The Eagle Mountain City Council will hold public hearings on June 16, 2026, at 7:00 PM or as soon thereafter as business allows, in the Eagle Mountain City Council Chambers, 1650 E Stagecoach Run, Eagle Mountain, Utah 84005.  The City Council will receive public comments concerning the following items:


FY 2026-2027 Interim Budget Adoption:

-	FY 2026-2027 Interim Budget Adoption: Eagle Mountain City will hold a Public Hearing at 7:00 PM, on Tuesday, June 16, 2026, to accept public comment on the 2026-2027 fiscal year Interim Budget. The Public Hearing will be held at the Eagle Mountain City Municipal Building located at 1650 E Stagecoach Run, Eagle Mountain, in the City Council Chambers. Public comment is welcome. The proposed budget can be viewed at eaglemountain.gov/finance and in the office of the Eagle Mountain City Recorder. 

The Interim Budget will be in effect for the period beginning on July 1, 2026, and ending after August 18, 2026, upon the City Council's adoption of a final budget. The fiscal year 2026-2027 tentative budget presented to the City Council on May 5, 2026, proposes a property tax increase triggering the Truth-In-Taxation process. The Interim Budget sets aside, in a restricted budget account the additional property tax revenue generated by the proposed tax rate increase. The City may not expend or otherwise obligate the restricted revenue until the completion of the Truth-In-Taxation process and the City Council has taken action to adopt a final budget for fiscal year 2026-2027 subject to the requirements of Utah Code Section 52-2-919.  To view the property tax impact schedule and learn more about the proposed tax increase, visit eaglemountain.gov/truth-in-taxation-property-tax. 
EMC Point of Contact: Director of Administrative Services, Kimberly Ruesch: kruesch@eaglemountain.gov.

GRANTSVILLE CITY
NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING
FISCAL YEAR 2027 TENTATIVE BUDGET


PUBLIC NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that the Grantsville City Council will hold a Public Hearing on Wednesday, June 3, 2026, at 7:00 p.m. for the purpose of receiving public input regarding the proposed Fiscal Year 2027 Tentative Budget and the adoption of the tentative budget on an interim basis pending final budget adoption. 

The Grantsville City Council will also consider a Resolution declaring the City's intent to consider an increase in property tax revenue above the certified tax rate for Fiscal Year 2027 and establishing the date, time, and place of the future Truth in Taxation public hearing required by Utah Code Section 59-2-919.

The public hearing will be held in person at Grantsville City Hall, located at 429 E. Main Street, Grantsville, Utah, 84029, and electronically via Zoom.

Public comments are welcome and may be provided in person during the meeting, or electronically using the following information:

Meeting URL: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/4358843411
Dial-In: 1-253-215-8782
Meeting ID: 435 884 3411

Written comments may also be submitted to the City Recorder, Alicia Fairbourne, at afairbourne@grantsvilleut.gov. All written comments will be distributed to the City Council and entered into the public record. To ensure consideration, written comments must be received no later than 12:00 p.m. (noon) on the day of the meeting.

Copies of the proposed tentative budget, proposed resolution, and Property Tax Impact Schedule may be reviewed during regular business hours at Grantsville City Hall or online at: https://www.grantsvilleut.gov/transparency/public_notices.php#outer-18sub-382, or on the Utah Public Notice website at https://www.utah.gov/pmn/sitemap/publicbody/1840.html. 


DATED this 22nd day of May, 2026.
Alicia Fairbourne
Grantsville City Recorder

title: Spanish Fork City Council Notice of the Fiscal Year 2027 Budget Public Hearing
Spanish Fork City Council Notice to Spanish Fork City Utility Customers 2027
agenda_text:
NOTICE TO SPANISH FORK CITY UTILITY CUSTOMERS

State law requires that the City provide an annual disclosure on funds transferred from a utility enterprise fund to any other fund. The City has budgeted the following transfers. 

The City of Spanish Fork has budgeted for the transfer from each utility fund to the general fund as a dividend to Spanish Fork taxpayers. This dividend is the result of the rate payers' investment in the City's utility infrastructure. These funds are used each year to help cover costs of important city services like police, fire, library, senior center, parks and recreation, and other city functions. The utility transfer helps keep property taxes low in Spanish Fork. If City utility services were provided by private utility vendors, these dividends would instead be paid to the private investor-owners. Because Spanish Fork residents are the investor-owners, these dividends are used to offset what otherwise would be a significant increase in property tax rates. These transfers are of funds which cannot be defined as a reasonable allocation of costs between funds. These amounts will not be repaid. 

The amounts of the transfers are as follows:	Dollar Amount          	% of Expenditures 
From the Power Fund to the General Fund	$ 1,310,000	  3.3 % From the Water Fund to the General Fund 	$ 352,000		2.6 % 
From the Sewer Fund to the General Fund	$ 152,000	0.9 %
From the Solid Waste Fund to the General Fund 	$ 50,000 	 1.3 % 
From the Broadband Fund to the General Fund 	$ 633,171 	  5.7 % 

Spanish Fork City also has a debt obligation that the Power Fund is helping make payments on. The funds are to pay for the Justice Center (Police/Court Building). This transfer is for funds which cannot be defined as a reasonable allocation of costs between funds. These amounts will not be repaid. 

The amount of this transfer is as follows:        	Dollar Amount	 % of Expenditures 
From the Power Fund to the Debt Service Fund 	$ 679,503 	1.7 %
